mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the previous two months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL annualized growth exceeds 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points over the previous month signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3pp.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the previous two months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator for economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where HOUST increases by more than 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous two months signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face increased costs and reduced output.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO decreases by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals robust consumer demand, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where RSAFS grows by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, it indicates a tight labor market with high interest rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to increased borrowing costs and reduced consumer spending.
regime_hint: tight monetary policy with low unemployment
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 5% and UNRATE < 4%.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 jobs in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 jobs and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.2pp.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter and housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% over the previous two months, it signals a strong demand environment, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 QoQ growth > 2% and HOUST increases > 5% in 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where GDPC1 grows by more than 2% QoQ and HOUST increases by more than 5%.
